docs.title: Canvas Features to Improve Your Workflow
docs.text:
The existing official Canvas documentation is bloated with outdated pages and unfinished stubs, making feature information difficult to locate. Third party guides typically only cover educator features and those designed for students bury advanced info in basic tutorials.

This user guide cuts through the excess. It skips basics (submitting assignments, checking grades, opening modules) and focuses on the settings and shortcuts that make Canvas more readable, easier to plan with, and faster to navigate.

:::info Note: Your institution controls which features are turned on. If a button or setting in this guide doesn't appear for you, it may be disabled for your school's Canvas account. :::

:::info

docs.title: Before You Start: The Sidebar
docs.text:
Every feature in this guide starts from the sidebar (Canvas calls it Global Navigation) along the left side of the screen. Hover over an icon to see its label.

:::info Note: If you don't see the sidebar, your screen may not be wide enough. To show the sidebar, click on the hamburger menu () on the top left of your screen. :::

Button Icon Description Used In Account Profile Portrait Accessibility Settings Dashboard Gauge Dashboard Views, Course Cards, To Dos Calendar Calendar Custom Events Inbox File Tray Canvas Inbox History Clock Recent History

:::info Note: The Canvas logo at the top left of the screen is also a button that routes to the Dashboard. :::

docs.title: Toggling Accessibility Settings
docs.text: Canvas has built-in display options that change how the entire interface looks — not just one page. They're tucked inside the Account menu, so most students never see them.

docs.title: Quick Toggles (Account Menu)
docs.text:
The two most common options can be switched on and off in one click.

  1. In the sidebar, click Account.
  2. Near the bottom of the menu that expands, find the toggles:
    • Use High Contrast UI — increases the contrast of text, buttons, and other interface elements so they're easier to distinguish.
    • Use a Dyslexia Friendly Font — switches the Canvas interface to the OpenDyslexic font.
  3. Click a toggle to turn it on. Refresh the browser page to see the change.

:::info Note: High Contrast UI hides institutional branding, so your school's logo and colors won't display while it's on. :::

docs.title: More Options (Feature Options)
docs.text:
More accessibility and comfort settings live one level deeper, in your user Settings.

  1. In the sidebar, click Account, then click Settings.
  2. Scroll down to the Feature Options section.
  3. Click the toggle next to any option you want to turn on.
Feature Option What It Does Auto Show Closed Captions Turns on captions by default for videos with captions added in Canvas (not YouTube or other third-party embeds). Disable Alert Notification Timeouts Keeps alert pop-ups on screen until you dismiss them, instead of letting them disappear. Disable Celebration Animations Turns off the confetti that appears when you submit an assignment on time. Only appears if your school has celebrations enabled. Disable Keyboard Shortcuts Turns off keyboard shortcuts in Modules and Discussions — useful if they conflict with a screen reader. Microsoft Immersive Reader Adds an Immersive Reader button to course home pages, assignments, pages, and the syllabus. Reads text aloud, adjusts spacing, and more. Underline Links Underlines links in menus, the Dashboard, and sidebars so they're easier to spot.

docs.title: Switching Between Card View and List View
docs.text:
The Dashboard can display your courses in more than one layout. Card View shows a tile for each course; List View shows a single, date-sorted agenda of everything due across all of your courses.

  1. In the sidebar, click Dashboard.
  2. At the top right of the Dashboard, click the Options icon (three vertical dots).
  3. Select a view:
    • Card View — one card per course. Best for jumping into a specific course.
    • List View — a scrolling agenda of assignments, quizzes, discussions, and to dos, grouped by date. Best for seeing what's due this week.
    • Recent Activity — a feed of recent announcements, discussions, and grading activity.

Canvas remembers your choice the next time you log in.

docs.title: Editing Course Cards
docs.text:
In Card View, every course card can be renamed, recolored, and rearranged. These changes are only visible to you — your instructor and classmates still see the original course.

All three options start in the same place: the Options icon (three vertical dots) in the top right corner of a course card.

docs.title: Nickname a Course
docs.text:
Course names generated by the registrar can be long and complicated (e.g., Site 3 Chem 1045 Fall 2024). A nickname replaces it with something readable.

Before Nicknamed After Nicknamed

To Nickname a course: 1. Click the card's Options icon. 2. In the Nickname field, type a new name (up to 59 characters). 3. Click Apply.

Nicknames appear on the Dashboard, in the course navigation menu, and in notification emails. To see the original course name, hover over the nickname.

To remove a nickname, delete the text in the Nickname field and click Apply.

docs.title: Change a Course Color
docs.text:
1. Click the card's Options icon.
  2. Click one of the color swatches, or type any color's hex code into the Hex Code field.
  3. Click Apply.

:::info Note: Course colors sync with the Calendar. If you color-code your courses here, your assignments in the Calendar will match. :::

docs.title: Move a Course Card
docs.text:
1. Click the card's Options icon.
  2. Click the Move tab.
  3. Choose where the card should go — to the top, before or after a specific card, or to the bottom.

You can also click and drag a card directly to a new spot on the Dashboard.

To remove a card from the Dashboard entirely, click Unfavorite in the Move tab. This option only appears if you've previously favorited courses.

docs.title: Show a Color Overlay
docs.text: If your instructor added a course image, the card color may be hidden behind it. To tint all image cards with their course colors, click the Dashboard's Options icon and select Color Overlay.

docs.title: Creating Custom To Dos from the Dashboard
docs.text:
Canvas automatically lists your assignments, but you can also add your own tasks (studying for an exam, meeting with a group, emailing a professor) so everything lives in one list.

  1. Switch the Dashboard to List View.
  2. At the top of the page, click the + (Add) to add a To Do.
  3. In the sidebar that opens, fill in the fields:
    • Title: the name of your task.
    • Date and Time: when you want to finish it. Time defaults to 11:59 PM.
    • Course: optional. Attach the task to a course, or leave it as a general To Do.
    • Details: any notes for yourself.
  4. Click Save.

Your To Do appears in the List View agenda with your profile picture next to it, so you can tell it apart from instructor-assigned work. It also appears in the To Do sidebar in Card View.

To edit or delete a To Do, click it, then click the Edit icon. Make your changes and click Save, or click Delete.

:::info Note: Tasks attached to a course show up alongside that course's assignments. Tasks without a course show up at the bottom of that day's list. :::

docs.title: Adding Custom Events to the Calendar
docs.text: The Calendar shows your course deadlines automatically, but it also has a personal calendar where you can add club meetings, shifts, office hours, and anything else.

docs.title: Add an Event
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, click Calendar.
  2. Click a date on the calendar, or click the + (Add) button at the top of the page.
  3. Make sure the Event tab is selected, then fill in the fields:
    • Title: The name of the event.
    • Date: Filled in automatically if you clicked a date.
    • From and To: The start and end time. Leave both blank to create an all-day event.
    • Frequency: Choose a repeat option (daily, weekly, etc.) to make it a recurring event.
    • Location: Optional.
    • Calendar: Make sure your personal calendar (your name) is selected.
  4. Click Submit.

To add a longer description or links, click More Options before submitting.

docs.title: Add a To Do from the Calendar
docs.text:
The Calendar can also create the same To Do's described in Creating Custom To Dos.

  1. Click the + (Add) button.
  2. Select the To Do tab.
  3. Enter a title, date, time, and (optionally) a calendar and details. If you add the To Do item to a specific course calendar, it will adopt that course's color coding.
  4. Click Submit.

docs.title: Show or Hide Course Calendars
docs.text:
The Calendar sidebar lists every course and group calendar. By default, only the first 10 are shown.

  • To hide or show a course's items, click the checkbox next to its name. Hidden calendars appear as faded text.
  • To change a course's color, hover over the course name, click the Options icon next to it, and choose a new color. This also changes the color of its course card.

:::info Note: Undated items at the bottom of the sidebar lists assignments and events that don't have a date yet. It's worth checking now and then. :::

docs.title: All Courses
docs.text: To view all of the courses you have been enrolled in since you were admitted as a student on Canvas, click Courses on the sidebar and select All Courses at the top of the list.

docs.title: Favorite
docs.text:
On the All Courses page, the Favorite indicates whether a course is favorited. A favorite course will have a yellow star.

Favorite courses will appear on your Dashboard, Courses list, and Calendar (if Course Calendar is toggled on).

:::warning Warning: If you unfavorite a course under Past Enrollments, you cannot favorite it again. :::

docs.title: Past Enrollments
docs.text:
You can view past courses and all of their content from the All Courses page.

  1. Scroll down until you reach the Past Enrollments heading.
  2. Click on a course's title to access it.

:::warning Warning: If you unfavorite a course under Past Enrollments, you cannot favorite it again. :::

docs.title: Sending Mail Through Canvas Inbox
docs.text: Canvas Inbox lets you message instructors, TAs, and classmates without looking up anyone's email address. Messages are tied to a course, so your instructor knows exactly which class you're writing about.

docs.title: Send a Message
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, click Inbox.
  2. Click the Compose icon (pencil and paper) at the top of the page.
  3. In the Course drop-down, select the course.
  4. In the To field, start typing a name, or click the Address Book icon to browse by role (Teachers, Students, Groups, etc.).
  5. Enter a Subject and type your message.
  6. (Optional) Click the Attach (paperclip) icon to add a file, or the Media icon to record or upload audio or video.
  7. Click Send.

:::warning Warning: When messaging more than one person, check the Send an individual message to each recipient box if you don't want everyone to see each other's replies. Otherwise, it sends as a group conversation. :::

:::info Note: You can't message users in a course after it has concluded. :::

docs.title: Find Messages Faster
docs.text:
• Filter by course: Use the course drop-down at the top of the Inbox to see only one class.
  • Filter by type: Switch between Inbox, Unread, Starred, Sent, Archived, and Submission Comments. Submission Comments collects every comment instructors have left on your assignments, across all courses.
  • Star: Hover over a conversation and click the star to flag it for later.
  • Search by user: Type a name to find every conversation with that person.

:::info Note: Right-click the Inbox link in the sidebar and open it in a new tab to keep your messages handy while you work elsewhere in Canvas. :::

docs.title: Navigating with Recent History
docs.text:
The History button keeps a running list of the course pages you've recently visited (assignments, pages, discussions, quizzes) so you can jump back without clicking through modules again.

  1. In the sidebar, click History (clock icon).
  2. A panel opens listing the pages you've viewed, newest first.
  3. Click any item to go straight to it.

Recent History holds up to three weeks of course page views.

:::info Note: History is especially useful when you remember reading something — a rubric, an announcement, an assignment prompt — but not which course or module it was in. :::

docs.title: Quick Links
docs.text:
If you've made it all the way here, and missed one of the topics, you can use the following table for a TL;DR instruction or click the links on the left to return to those sections.

I want to... Then do... Make Canvas easier to read Account → Use High Contrast UI / Use a Dyslexia Friendly Font Turn on captions, underlined links, or Immersive Reader Account → Settings → Feature Options Timeline of everything due across all courses Dashboard → Options (⋮) → List View Rename, recolor, or reorder a course Dashboard (Card View) → card's Options (⋮) Add my own task Dashboard (List View) → Add To Do Add a personal event Calendar → + → Event Add/Remove a course from my Dashboard Courses → All Courses → Toggle Favorite Revisit a completed Canvas course Courses → All Courses → Scroll down to Past Enrollments Message my instructor/classmate Inbox → Compose → select course → To Find a page I visited earlier History
